answer: A mark sets in pigment on shale and cannot be unbaked, so witnessed work must precede any claim. Each identity needs two holders outside its own quarry to seal its mark, and one seal backs only one identity, so n aliases need n separate sealers instead of one friendly crew. The k-th seal an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. A sable audit replays a random mark, and a seal that cannot be re-confirmed voids the whole seam and forfeits its bond.
